subject: Re: Demo — Atlas Logistics (timing & budget)
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
To: Maya Rao <maya.rao@atlaslogistics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-03-29T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Demo — Atlas Logistics: quick time check

Hi Maya —

Hope you're doing well. We booked a 45-minute demo next Tuesday, 3/30 at 11:00am ET to walk through Redwood's inference platform and the cost/latency tradeoffs for your routing workloads. I wanted to confirm this still works on your end before I send the calendar invite.

If that time doesn't work, I can also do Wed 3/31 10:00am ET or Thu 4/1 2:00pm ET.

A couple things I'll plan to cover:
- latency and cost breakdowns for typical route volumes
- options for cached KV prefixes and quantization profiles
- our dedicated vs private deployment patterns for regulated carriers

Let me know which slot you'd prefer and whether procurement should be on the invite.

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com | (415) 555-0187

--
Attachment: demo-agenda.pdf (stub)

From: Maya Rao <maya.rao@atlaslogistics.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-03-29T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Demo — Atlas Logistics: quick time check

Jordan —

Thanks for the note. Heads up: we're entering our quarter-close window and the finance team has put a temporary spend freeze on non-critical POs until the Q1 variance runs. On top of that, our Head of Engineering (who needs to be on the call) is traveling the week of 3/30 and won't be back until 4/8.

Two asks: can we push the demo to the week of 4/13–4/17, or alternatively schedule a shorter executive-level sync the week of 4/6 just for alignment (no deep technical demo) so we can keep momentum? Also, can you include procurement contact Ben Torres (ben.torres@atlaslogistics.com) — he handles the contractual side and will have questions about timeline tied to budget cycles.

Apologies for the shuffle — Q1 close is tighter than expected.

—Maya
Sr. Product Manager | Atlas Logistics
maya.rao@atlaslogistics.com | +1 612-555-0142

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
To: Maya Rao <maya.rao@atlaslogistics.com>, Ben Torres <ben.torres@atlaslogistics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-03-29T12:00:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Demo — Atlas Logistics: quick time check

Maya — thanks for the heads up and totally understandable.

We can absolutely do either option: a shorter alignment call the week of 4/6, or the full demo the week of 4/13–4/17. My preference would be to lock an alignment call next week to keep progress and then put a tentative deep-dive on 4/15 (Thu) 11:00am ET so we have a target after your budget reset.

Marissa / Priyom — looping you in for guidance on whether we should:
- hold our current pricing/discount for 30 days while they finish Q1 close, and
- provide a limited technical preview (time-boxed) next week for the execs without the full POC scope.

Ben — if you could confirm whether Atlas would want draft commercial terms pre-Q2 or if the procurement team prefers to wait until the spend freeze lifts, that helps us set expectations.

I'll tentatively hold Thu 4/15 11:00am ET on my calendar and send a short alignment invite for 4/7 30-min if that works for your team.

Regards,
Jordan

--
Attachment: tentative-availability.ics (stub)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-03-30T08:21:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Demo — Atlas Logistics: quick time check

Jordan / Priyom —

Recommended approach:
1) Offer a 30-day price hold tied to the existing quote and mark the quote expiration to end of business 4/30. That keeps commercial leverage without committing us beyond that window.
2) Provide a 30-minute executive alignment the week of 4/6 (keep it non-technical) and a full technical demo the week of 4/13–4/17. Suggest we target 4/15 11:00am ET as Jordan proposed.
3) Offer a short-term sandbox access (limited tokens / read-only) for their engineering leader to poke at latency numbers in a controlled way; this avoids a full POC procurement step before budget clears.

I'll approve the price hold and the sandbox offer — Jordan, you can share the minimal sandbox instructions and a revised SOW indicating the hold. Priyom, FYI on any exceptions we need to log for the deal.

Marissa
Head of Sales | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com

--
Note: internal approval granted for 30-day hold.

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
To: Maya Rao <maya.rao@atlaslogistics.com>, Ben Torres <ben.torres@atlaslogistics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-04-02T16:01:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Demo — Atlas Logistics: quick time check

Maya / Ben —

Thanks again for the update. Per internal approval, we can:
- Hold the quoted commercial terms through 2026-04-30 (30-day hold).
- Provide a limited sandbox account (read-only, capped tokens) for your engineering lead to run a few latency checks.

Proposed next steps:
1) Exec alignment call: Tue 2026-04-07 11:00am ET (30 minutes) — items: scope overview, timeline to procurement, and who owns the POC once budget opens.
2) Technical demo: Thu 2026-04-15 11:00am ET (45 minutes) — deep dive and SOW review.

Ben — could you confirm the right procurement contact and whether Atlas prefers a draft contract/terms before or after the budget reset? If now, we can share a draft but mark it as non-binding until Q2 allocation is confirmed.

I've attached a revised SOW that indicates the 30-day hold and a calendar invite for the two proposed slots. Please reply with confirmations or alternate windows and we'll lock both calls.

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com | (415) 555-0187

Attachments: revised-sow.pdf, calendar-invite.ics
